stdin.note: The dedicated server runs with a console window. Valve's community guide starts it as 'srcds.exe -console -game dota +map dota' (Windows) or './srcds_run -game dota +map dota' (Linux); FireDaemon's KB and TimZaman/dotaservice start it as '-dedicated -game dota +map dota', dotaservice via dota.sh. dotaservice records that this console takes typed commands ('restart' restarts the game, 'quit' exits), so a command channel exists - but that the channel is the process's stdin is inferred from how srcds_run/dota.sh are driven, not stated by any source found. Valve publishes no admin command reference for it.

notes: No commands are recorded on purpose. The server exists and has a console - app 580 is named 'DotA 2 Dedicated Server' by Valve, and every guide found starts a '-game dota' process and talks to it through that console - but no source, Valve's or otherwise, documents a list-players, kick, ban or broadcast command for it, and inventing plausible Source-engine ones would be a guess. Cautions. (1) The launch line differs by source: the Steam community guide shows 'srcds.exe -console -game dota +map dota' with no -dedicated, while FireDaemon and dotaservice show '-dedicated -game dota +map dota'; dotaservice drives dota.sh rather than srcds_run, so 'srcds' naming is the pre-Reborn spelling. (2) Dota 2 moved from Source 1 to Source 2 with Reborn in 2015; every page showing a server.cfg with rcon_password (the RaGEZONE thread) and every Metamod/SourceMod route (psychonic/d2fixups, archived 2022) predates or was broken by that move, so transport is recorded as the console, not rcon - a Source RCON listener on the current build is unconfirmed. (3) Moderation on a Dota 2 server is not a console job: matches are lobbies whose membership the Game Coordinator controls, so the lobby host kicks through the in-game UI. (4) appId is the dedicated-server app 580 as Valve names it, but the server FILES install from app 570 ('dota 2 beta') and FireDaemon's steamcmd line needs a real login, not anonymous - 580 is not what SteamCMD downloads. Treat this file as 'console exists, command text unknown', not as 'unsupported'; the host-level floor is the right fallback.
